claims.text: The unresolved stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr originates from nanoscale compositional fluctuations.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations create local differences in thermal expansion.
Differential contraction during cooling from solidification generates residual thermal stresses.
The resulting residual stresses influence dislocation mobility and defect interactions.
Residual thermal stresses modify creep behavior.
Residual thermal stresses modify strain hardening during deformation.
Residual thermal stresses modify the alloy's elastic and thermoelastic responses.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr contains nanoscale compositional inhomogeneities.
The as-cast alloy contains local thermal-expansion variations and associated residual stresses.
High-temperature solution annealing followed by controlled slow cooling will minimize local compositional fluctuations relative to the as-cast state.
The homogenized material will have lower residual stress than the as-cast baseline.
Reduced residual stress in the homogenized material will increase the creep rate at 1250 °C.
The homogenized material will exhibit less hardening after identical cold rolling.
The homogenized material will show smoother and more predictable temperature-dependent elastic moduli.
The homogenized material will show smoother and more nearly linear thermal-expansion behavior.
The proposed mechanistic effects will be most significant between 600 °C and 1250 °C.
Homogenization-induced changes in defect density or grain size could also affect the measured mechanical and thermoelastic properties.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify thermal-expansion measurements from 600 °C to 1250 °C, whereas the falsification design specifies elastic-modulus and thermal-expansion data over 293–1250 K. These are materially different ranges: 1250 K is about 977 °C, not 1250 °C.
